data.narrative:
Phaidra is a Series B artificial intelligence and software company founded by Jim Gao (former head of industrial AI at Google DeepMind), Vedavyas Panneershelvam (primary engineer on AlphaGo), and Katherine Hoffman (former Trane Technologies and Raytheon operations lead). The company has raised $120M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 private companies and 1 public company (Palantir) operating in the same sector and stage.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method, using $120M in total raised as a proxy for current valuation and applying a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B-to-next-stage step-ups, yields $228M. The peer-median method examines four same-sector, same-stage comparables: Scale AI ($29.0B), Physical Intelligence ($5.6B), Black Forest Labs ($3.2B), and Field AI ($2.0B). The median of this peer set is $4.4B, with a range of $2.0B to $29.0B.

Triangulating these two methods produces a valuation range of $194M to $5.1B, with a median of $2.3B. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around whether Phaidra's technology and market position align closer to earlier-stage comparables (stage-progression floor) or to high-valuation peers like Physical Intelligence and Scale AI. Key uncertainties include revenue traction, customer concentration, and market timing. The median estimate of $2.3B reflects balanced treatment of both methodologies.
